item.title: French Montana’s Amsterdam, Vienna Concerts Suddenly Canceled
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: French Montana and D-Block Europe's October 30 Amsterdam show was canceled, with Ticketmaster set to contact ticket holders.
item.content:encoded:
French Montana and D-Block Europe’s Amsterdam concert was canceled, leaving fans without the joint show booked for Friday, October 30, at AFAS Live.

The venue confirmed the cancellation on its official event page, citing “unforeseen circumstances.”

“Ticket holders will receive an email from Ticketmaster with further information regarding the cancellation,” AFAS Live said.

The Amsterdam stop was billed as part of the “Worldwide Wave Tour.” Their London date remains on sale.

London’s O2 still lists D-Block Europe with French Montana as a special guest for Wednesday, October 28. The arena’s event page shows tickets on sale through AXS, its official ticket partner. Doors are listed for 6:30 P.M.

Another canceled date on Ticketmaster’s French Montana calendar is the November 6 show with D-Block Europe at Raiffeisen Halle im Gasometer in Vienna. That listing marks the Austrian concert as canceled without giving a reason.

Young Adz and Dirtbike LB formed D-Block Europe in Lewisham, London. They had come close to topping the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart with The Blue Print – Us Vs. Them and Lap 5. Both albums peaked at No. 2.

The duo reached No. 1 in January 2024 with Rolling Stone, their third studio album. It featured Yxng Bane, Noizy and Kodak Black. That success brought their Top 10 album tally to eight at the time, according to Official Charts.

That week, Rolling Stone also led the U.K. sales chart for independent record stores. It entered the vinyl albums chart at No. 2, giving the pair a strong showing with record buyers, too.

French Montana’s recent work also revisited a longtime partnership.

He and Max B announced Wave Gods 2: Cosmos Brothers earlier this year, with a May 22 release, as AllHipHop reported on their reunion. That project included “Smoking Part 2” and reunited two artists who had made music together years before.

French Montana explained that the album’s title grew from Max B’s talk about cosmic energy during calls between the two artists. He also described the music he wanted to make: “I’m all about restoration. I felt like the music business lost that edge, lost that music that people appreciated.”

item.title: Lewis Hamilton Reveals Dog Gift For Kanye & Kim Kardashian’s Four Kids
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lewis Hamilton said he gave Kim Kardashian's four children a dog named Halo as he shared what brought him joy away from racing.
item.content:encoded:
Lewis Hamilton gave Kim Kardashian‘s four children a dog this year. His name is Halo, and the driver called him part of the family. The Formula 1 star shared the news when asked what brought him joy outside of racing.

Hamilton, 41, spoke at a press panel in Austin, Texas, on Saturday, October 24. He was in town for the F1 Grand Prix. He first mentioned the joy his niece and nephew bring him. He then turned to his girlfriend’s kids and said he loved spending time with them.

“I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family,” he said.

Kardashian shares North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8 and Psalm, 7, with her former husband, Kanye West. The children have also appeared in photos with Hamilton as his relationship with their mother became more public over the summer.

In July, Hamilton posted a photo of himself with Kardashian, Chicago and Psalm. The group posed together by a lake on a summer trip.

Fans had seen Halo in the couple’s social media posts before the Austin event. According to HOLA!, Kardashian shared a photo of herself holding the golden retriever on July 30. Hamilton joined Kardashian and her family on that lakeside trip.

On September 22, Hamilton posted another photo of Halo. This time, the dog had its front paws up on a gate.

The couple’s family outings followed a friendship that became a romance earlier this year. Us Weekly reported that Kardashian introduced Hamilton to her children as the two began dating after knowing each other for years.

For Kardashian, the relationship came after a period she set aside to heal. She said she wanted to put her kids and work first. She told The Times she had felt no rush to date again. She had enjoyed having that space for herself.

Kardashian filed for divorce from West in February 2021. They reached a settlement in November 2022. By June 2026, she was spending more time with Hamilton online. That month, she posted a photo and video from their New York bike ride.

item.title: Drake Honors Lil Wayne At Birthday Party, But Is A Major Reunion Coming?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Drake's emotional birthday tribute to Lil Wayne raises fresh questions about their unreleased collaborations and whether the legendary duo could reunite.
item.content:encoded:
Drake turned 40 over the weekend, but his birthday tribute to Lil Wayne has me wondering whether the next chapter of their legendary partnership is finally approaching.

The Toronto-based superstar celebrated his milestone birthday with lavish festivities in New York City, surrounded by famous friends, family and luxury. But amid the random things happening, Drake got sentimental.

READ ALSO: Drake Turns 40: 40 Things I’ve Learned From Drake

First, he shared a musical moment with his father, Dennis Graham, who arrived sporting a colorful outfit and a parrot on his shoulder. Yes, an actual parrot. Apparently, ordinary birthday accessories are beneath the Graham family.

The father and son performed together, with Dennis revisiting his 2017 song “Kinda Crazy.” It was a touching family moment. That bird deserves an honorable mention.

Then came the big tribute.

“I would not be here if it was not by way and courtesy of the young man Lil Wayne from YMCMB.”

Wayne wasn’t present, but his chi certainly was.

And here’s why I’m paying attention.

Earlier this month, Weezy revealed that he and Drake have a substantial collection of unreleased recordings, including material dating back to 2014 and 2015.

“We have a whole bunch of unreleased material. I go through stuff from 2014 and 2015, like… really unheard stuff,” Wayne said. “I edit stuff up and just send it to his phone so he can hear the new versions of it and get him going.”

Wayne also indicated that Drake has been enthusiastic about potentially releasing those recordings.

READ ALSO: Loe Shimmy Gifts Drake A 1986 Ferrari For His 40th Birthday

Between 2008 and 2013, the two delivered an extraordinary collection of collaborations, including “Miss Me,” “She Will,” “The Motto” and “HYFR.” Wayne helped introduce Drake to the masses, and Drake eventually ascended into global superstardom.

Their last released collaborations arrived in 2021, when they appeared on Nicki Minaj’s “Seeing Green” and Drake’s “You Only Live Twice” alongside Rick Ross.

That’s five years without another major musical reunion.

Could Drake’s birthday reflection signal renewed interest in those unreleased recordings? Perhaps. There’s no confirmed album, single or release date, but Wayne’s recent comments suggest the music remains very much alive.

And personally, I’d rather hear those vintage recordings than watch another round of internet arguments about who won some rap beef.

At 40, Drake has accomplished virtually everything commercially. Revisiting his musical roots with Wayne could provide something those streaming records cannot.

A reunion with the man who helped make it all possible.

Now, somebody please convince Weezy to open that vault.

item.title: El Paso NAACP Condemns Halloween KKK Imagery
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: The El Paso NAACP urged local leaders to condemn KKK imagery after people dressed as Klansmen appeared in social media posts.
item.content:encoded:
El Paso’s NAACP demanded that local leaders condemn KKK imagery after images of people dressed as Klansmen circulated online.

The El Paso Times reported that clips showed about six people in white robes in a backyard and walking down a neighborhood street. FitFam El Paso identified the area as the East Side. The gathering appeared to be a Halloween event.

“The KKK hood is not a costume,” the branch said in a Sunday, October 25, statement reported by KTSM. Branch President Carl B. Dwyer Jr. added: “Silence in the face of hatred is complicity.”

Rep. Veronica Escobar also condemned the images Sunday. Her statement described reports of people in Klan clothing allegedly shouting racial slurs as “deeply disturbing and unacceptable.”

Pastor Michael Grady told KTSM that hatred was learned and said he wanted to ask the participants about their motives. He said the display reflected a national climate of division and discrimination.

The branch called on elected officials, faith leaders and civic advocates across El Paso County to speak out against the display.

The robes carry a long history of violence in Texas. The Texas State Historical Association traces Klan activity in the state to 1868. By that spring, members were murdering and terrorizing formerly enslaved people and White Republicans.

In Trinity County, masked groups killed Black residents and used fear to control how others registered to vote. The later Klan revival drew tens of thousands of Texans in the early 1920s, with hooded marches and burning crosses used to display its power.

That history also reached El Paso’s public institutions. KFOX14/CBS4 reported in February that the local historical society documented Klan control of the school board between 1921 and 1923. The group’s local campaign also targeted Catholics. An anti-Klan ticket led by Richard Dudley won the 1923 mayoral race, the report said.

The public response to Klan imagery has reached major brands, too. AllHipHop reported on Converse’s apology in September after viewers said advertisements recalled Klan hoods and lynching.

The company removed the image and acknowledged it was upsetting.

The El Paso NAACP planned a news conference for Monday, October 26, to address the incident.

item.title: Mary J. Blige Partners With Primary Wave
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mary J. Blige partnered with Primary Wave on her music catalog as the company pursued new opportunities for her songs.
item.content:encoded:
Mary J. Blige partnered with Primary Wave Music on her catalog, bringing both her compositions and recordings into the agreement.

The company will work with Blige’s team on marketing, branding, digital projects and music licensing opportunities, Billboard reported. The deal includes songs such as “Family Affair,” “Be Without You” and “I Can Love You.”

The available reports did not disclose a price or ownership percentage.

The partnership concerns a career that took shape at Uptown Records. Blige signed with Andre Harrell’s label in 1989 at age 18.

Her 1992 debut, What’s the 411?, put her voice over a mix of Hip-Hop and soul, with personal lyrics at the center. “You Remind Me” and “Real Love” were among its hits. Her official biography lists Aretha Franklin, Chaka Khan and Gladys Knight among the singers who influenced her early on.

That musical history matters to the catalog beyond the record titles. Her second album, 1994’s My Life, drew from older soul while speaking to the sound of its own time. The Library of Congress added it to the National Recording Registry in 2025.

She wrote most of the lyrics, taking a larger role in shaping the album’s personal stories. Producer Charles “Chucky” Thompson helped build the sound around her.

Her catalog has remained part of her live work, too.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Blige announced her first Las Vegas residency at Dolby Live at Park MGM earlier this year. The original plan called for 10 performances, split between May and July.

She said she had long wanted to do that kind of show. The residency, which began in May, had been extended through 2027.

item.title: Macklemore Faces UK Ban Push From 50 Peers Before Wembley Benefit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Macklemore faced calls from 50 peers to block his UK entry before a Wembley benefit, days after his Red Rocks return.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore faces a push from 50 House of Lords members to bar him from Britain before his October 30 benefit concert.

The group asked Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to revoke his electronic travel authorization, according to Metro, which cited a letter The Telegraph reported.

Baron Walney, a former government adviser on political violence, wrote the letter, which objected to the Palestinian Youth Movement receiving some of the concert’s proceeds.

The peers accused the organization of links to terrorist groups and glorifying terrorism, allegations the Palestinian Youth Movement denied.

Metro said it sought comment from Macklemore and the Home Office, but its report included no response or decision revoking his permission to travel.

The entry demand followed his October 22 return to the stage at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, where he again spoke up for Palestinians before a Colorado crowd.

“Being a human being in this moment is not complicated,” Macklemore said. “It is not political.”

He also addressed suffering beyond Gaza, speaking about Sudan, Congo, Lebanon and Haiti as well as people afraid of ICE in America.

“The message will always be love,” Macklemore told the Red Rocks audience.

Red Rocks was his first performance since losing the rest of his appearances as Ed Sheeran’s opening act. That dispute followed his September appearances at MetLife Stadium, where he publicly advocated for Palestinians.

New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft objected to Macklemore performing at Gillette Stadium, citing rhetoric and imagery he considered offensive to Jewish people. Macklemore distinguished his criticism of Israel from criticism of Jewish people and called for equal treatment.

Sheeran said the tour’s organizers made the decision and later apologized for how he handled the dispute during a Philadelphia concert.

The Wembley event page for “Macklemore & Friends: Free Palestine Tour” lists 12 beneficiaries, including the Palestinian Youth Movement, Medical Aid for Palestinians and UNRWA USA.

It says all proceeds will support the listed groups, whose work spans medical treatment, education, humanitarian relief and advocacy. The page does not specify how the money will be split among the 12 listed organizations.

The benefit series is due in Dublin on October 26, Paris on October 29 and then London.

item.title: Ye Defends Jakarta Crowd After “Heartless” Clip Draws Criticism
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ye praised his Jakarta audience after a "Heartless" clip drew claims that he was trying to provoke fans during the concert.
item.content:encoded:
Ye praised his Jakarta crowd after a clip of him restarting “Heartless” led to claims that he was trying to get a rise out of fans. The rapper’s own account of the night was far warmer than the criticism suggested.

Ye responded on X to a user who shared the performance and accused him of provoking the audience. The outlet reported that he repeated part of the song seven times while getting fans to sing along.

“Bro. This shit was a vibe. The crowd was very loud. It’s called rock and roll,” Ye wrote.

He posted the response Sunday, October 25, a day after the concert. Medcom reported that the show began at 9 P.M. and was promoted by Raw Vision Collective. It was his first solo concert in Indonesia.

The show took place Saturday, October 24 at Gelora B### Karno Stadium. Jakarta Globe’s account described a “Heartless” performance in which Ye had the audience handle the chorus. At one point, fans sang without the backing track. Their voices became part of the performance, with Ye asking them to return to the refrain.

Elsewhere in the set, the audience heard older songs including “All Falls Down,” “Through the Wire” and “Gold Digger.”

The roughly two-hour concert put Ye on a huge globe-shaped stage with fans around it, while lasers and fireworks filled out the production.

Organizers estimated attendance at 50,000, according to Jakarta Globe. Fans also offered different views of the sound. One reported rough audio at times, while another said it was clear overall from his seat, with some speaker vibrations overlapping.

AllHipHop previously reported the Jakarta booking in July. It was announced as the only Southeast Asian stop on his 2026 tour. It was also his first performance in the region in more than 15 years.

His earlier visits included Singapore shows in 2008 and 2010, giving the Jakarta date a place in a much longer gap between regional appearances.

The night closed with another chance for fans to sing. For “Runaway,” Ye returned with a small piano after going inside the globe. Fireworks accompanied the song’s opening notes as the crowd joined in.

item.title: Chicago Musicians Call For Two-Day Streaming Boycott Over AI
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Spotify and other streaming services drew a two-day boycott call from Chicago musicians protesting AI-generated music.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago musicians asked listeners to skip Spotify and other music-streaming services on October 26 and 27 as they pushed back against AI-made music.

The call came at a rally in Federal Plaza, according to photographer Jack Siegel, who attended and documented the protest. He counted about 20 musicians, including blues guitarist Melody Angel and jazz singer Tammy McCann.

McCann argued that a machine could not draw on the human experiences behind a song. Angel spoke about music’s power to connect people and the risk of losing that bond.

The boycott dates follow a fresh Spotify update on AI content.

In its October 20 announcement, the company said it had blocked more than 50 million tracks it classed as slop or spam from recommendations this year. Those songs were kept out of suggestions, a different step from removing a recording from the service altogether.

The company said its checks combine listener feedback, upload patterns and third-party AI detectors.

The company also cited more than 75 million tracks removed for serious or repeated rule violations.

Its tools draw a line between an AI artist identity and AI use within a recording. Spotify said its AI Persona badges flag identities it believes were made with AI.

By default, those profiles are excluded from editorial and automated recommendations, with exceptions such as a listener choosing to follow one.

Separate AI Credits let artists disclose which roles and instruments involved AI. Listeners can find those details in a song’s credits on the mobile app, the company said.

Meanwhile, AllHipHop previously reported that Spotify’s deal with Believe would let participating artists choose whether to allow paid AI covers and remixes. Saying yes to hearing about AI plans would still leave an artist free to reject that tool.

Spotify also said artists in its Profile Protection test could review releases submitted under their names. It planned to make that safeguard available to all artists by the end of the year.

item.title: Samuel L. Jackson Gets Profane In Karen Bass Election Push
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Samuel L. Jackson urged Los Angeles voters to reelect Karen Bass in a profane campaign video ahead of her November 3 runoff.
item.content:encoded:
Samuel L. Jackson brought a profane voting plea to Karen Bass’ reelection push as the Los Angeles mayor faced City Councilmember Nithya Raman in the November 3 runoff.

The actor backed Bass in a new campaign video released Sunday, October 25. He defended her work on homelessness and argued that running a citywide response was tougher than testing a program in one district.

“Vote, motherf*****!” Jackson said. His message also criticized Raman’s handling of homelessness committee meetings.

Several other actors made their own cases for Bass. Anthony Anderson pointed to her work on California’s film and television tax credit in a Saturday video. Jane Fonda praised her years as an organizer and public official, while Cedric the Entertainer drew on his long relationship with Bass.

“She is the right person for the job,” Cedric said in his video, the Post reported.

Jackson had also publicly backed Bass months earlier in this year’s race. In that earlier endorsement, The National News Desk reported in May that he stressed her knowledge of government and ability to bring people together. Bass described him as a friend who shared her housing and crime goals.

The profanity also fit an approach Jackson had used to promote voting before. During the 2020 presidential election, he offered fans lessons in swearing in 15 languages through HeadCount’s nonpartisan Good to Vote effort.

That challenge called for 2,500 people to take a voting action through his link. Celebrity participants offered fans special access or rewards tied to participation, putting Jackson’s famous vocabulary to work for voter outreach six years before this mayoral appeal.

Housing policy remained a central divide in the current contest. HousingWire reported that groups pushing for more home construction backed Raman. She favored faster construction and opposed the city’s delay in carrying out state housing requirements near transit.

Governor Gavin Newsom, labor groups and much of the city’s Democratic establishment supported Bass. Raman also drew labor and progressive endorsements, giving voters a choice between two candidates with different plans to ease Los Angeles’ housing shortage.

Election Day was set for November 3.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Fights Against Child Sex Changes
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj urged adults to leave children out of transgender issues while campaigning for Republicans at Donald Trump's Michigan rally.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj made transgender issues involving children part of her pitch for Michigan Republicans during her appearance at Donald Trump’s Port Huron rally.

“We don’t want our children to be bombarded with sex changes. Leave the children alone. Leave them out of it,” Minaj said.

The rapper spoke at McMorran Place Arena in Port Huron on Sunday, October 25. Thousands attended the event, which came nine days before the November 3 midterm election.

Her comments about children formed part of a broader appeal for conservative votes. Nicki Minaj stressed Michigan’s importance in national elections and urged supporters to keep working for the future they wanted for their children.

She also led the crowd in chants for Mike Rogers, the Republican running for U.S. Senate, and John James, the party’s gubernatorial candidate. Rogers faced Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, while James faced Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson.

Trump also asked supporters to turn out even though he was not on the ballot. The Republican rally followed former President Barack Obama’s Detroit campaign stop on Saturday.

Obama urged Democrats to offer concrete plans to reduce living costs, including healthcare and housing, as both parties courted Michigan voters before Election Day.

The trip had already given Minaj another chance to explain her support for Trump. Earlier Sunday, she spoke with White House communications director Steven Cheung aboard Air Force One as she traveled to Michigan with the president.

As AllHipHop previously reported, she praised Trump’s approach to international negotiations and said his financial setbacks helped explain her confidence in his economic plans. Cheung also asked about his work habits, which she praised during the exchange.

The rally’s discussion of children and medical care touched a policy issue in the Senate race Minaj was promoting. El-Sayed’s healthcare platform said patients and doctors should make personal healthcare decisions, with parents involved when the patient was a minor.

His campaign expressly included gender-affirming and reproductive care in that position. The platform also opposed efforts to criminalize medications or use lawsuits and funding cuts to prevent providers from delivering care.
